title: FEDERAL RESEARCH: Additional Actions Needed to Improve Monitoring of Grant Performance
document:
SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Federal agencies obligate billions of dollars annually on research grants to universities, nonprofit research institutions, and small businesses. In fiscal year 2020, five key grant-making agencies obligated approximately $42 billion across more than 45,000 active research awards. Effective monitoring of these awards is critical to ensuring that taxpayer funds are used as intended and research milestones are achieved.

SECTION 2: KEY FINDINGS
Our review of 120 randomly selected research grants across the Department of Energy (DOE), National Science Foundation (NSF), and National Institutes of Health (NIH) identified significant inconsistencies in how performance progress reports are tracked and evaluated. Specifically, 34 percent of reviewed grant files lacked documentation showing that program managers conducted formal performance reviews within the mandatory 90-day post-award period.
Furthermore, two of the three agencies did not maintain centralized databases to capture technical deliverables, resulting in fragmented oversight. When technical deviations were reported by researchers, agency staff took an average of 142 days to initiate corrective action discussions.

SECTION 3: RISKS IDENTIFIED
1. Compliance Risk: Incomplete monitoring records create substantial vulnerability to grant non-compliance and misallocation of federal research funds.
2. Timeline Risk: Delays in reviewing annual milestone reports impede early detection of failing research protocols, potentially resulting in millions spent on non-viable studies.
3. Data Integrity Risk: Decentralized document retention practices prevent cross-agency collaboration and increase the risk of duplicate funding across peer agencies.

SECTION 4: DECISIONS MADE
- The Office of Federal Financial Management has established an inter-agency working group to standardize grant reporting metrics across STEM programs.
- Agency leadership at NSF agreed to implement an automated milestone alert system by Q4 2022.

SECTION 5: RECOMMENDATIONS
GAO makes four primary recommendations:
1. The Secretary of Energy should direct program offices to establish written guidelines requiring formal review memos for all annual progress submissions.
2. The Director of NSF should integrate technical milestone tracking into the agency's enterprise financial management system.
3. The Director of NIH should mandate annual training for grant officers focusing on protocol deviation escalation procedures.
4. All three agencies should coordinate with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to develop common digital reporting schemas for research deliverables.

SECTION 6: ACTION ITEMS & TIMELINES
- Action Item 1: Publish revised grant monitoring guidance by October 1, 2021 (Responsible: DOE Grants Policy Division).
- Action Item 2: Deploy Phase 1 automated compliance tracking dashboard by January 15, 2022 (Responsible: NSF Office of Information Systems).
- Action Item 3: Conduct audit of outstanding technical deliverables for awards exceeding $5 million by December 31, 2021 (Responsible: NIH Inspector General).
summary: Federal agencies obligate over $42 billion annually for research grants, but monitoring remains inconsistent across major grant-making bodies. GAO analyzed 120 grant files at DOE, NSF, and NIH, discovering that 34 percent lacked timely performance review documentation and agencies experienced average delays of 142 days when addressing technical deviations. Major risks include compliance failures, milestone delays, and duplicate funding. GAO recommends mandatory written review guidelines, enterprise milestone integration, enhanced grant officer training, and coordinated digital reporting standards under OMB oversight.
